$comment: Resolved content baselines for the federated entries in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
Deliberately NOT stored in marketplace.json: that file is consumed by Claude Code
against its own marketplace schema, and must not carry keys the plugin loader does
not expect. This sidecar is read only by scripts/check-federated-content.mjs.
Why it exists: a federated entry pins a tag by NAME, and a tag name is mutable.
Re-pointing it at different content is silent - every consumer follows, and the
existing pin check still passes because it only asks whether the tag resolves and
declares the matching version. lore-cli and quest-cli both had v0.6.0 deleted and
recreated on 2026-09-10/11 (OMARK-43); the skill content happened to be unchanged,
but nothing in CI could have told us if it had not been.
To update: re-resolve the chain yourself (tag ref -> tag object -> commit -> root
tree -> skills subtree), confirm the content is what you intend to ship, and record
the new SHA here in the same change that moves the pin. Updating this file is the
act of saying 'I verified this content', so do not update it to make CI go green.
Release handshake, agreed with the lore-cli session and tracked there as LCLI-469:
lore-cli messages this repository at tag-cut time with the tag name, the tag object
SHA, the commit it peels to, and the resolved skills/ tree SHA, so a new release
arrives with its baseline rather than as a red check here. The same is expected of
quest-cli. Do not take those SHAs on trust - they are a head start, not a
verification; re-resolve them here before recording, which is the whole point of
this file. If a pin bump ever lands without its baseline moving, the checker fails
on purpose rather than silently checking the wrong tag.

proof-skills.note: OMARK-73, dispatched by opum-agent (OPAG-437, operator ruling 2026-09-25: MIT-license and publish proof-skills under Opum AI). First pin of a fourth, non-federated-by-history plugin -- proof-skills is a new public repo, not a spin-off of an existing pin. Layout question (a git-subdir source into plugins/proof-skills/ vs. repo-root) was measured against this repository's own check-federated-pins.mjs, check-federated-content.mjs, and generate-codex-marketplace.mjs: none handle git-subdir without a code change (classifyEntry hardcodes source==='github'; resolveSubtree only walks one level into the root tree; generate-codex-marketplace.mjs's own test already locks in 'throw on git-subdir'), and Codex's per-plugin source has no documented subdirectory field. opum-agent ruled repo-root. v0.1.0 (the plugins/proof-skills/ subdir layout) shipped and stays published, unpinned here, and is never re-cut -- re-pointing it would be the exact tag-mutation shape OMARK-43 exists to catch. v0.1.1 ships the layout moved to the repo root instead, as a new tag. Tag chain resolved independently via the GitHub API and cross-checked via git ls-remote --tags (not taken from opum-agent's relay): v0.1.1 is an ANNOTATED tag -> tag object eb96f9681363f34d369612059814e17a300afd8f -> peels to commit 578749fd8baa6456d89d7a0037c88bc09a89213d, which is also the repository's main HEAD (confirmed via git/ref/heads/main) -> root tree 9a53258d828aee4b8d474b6428f8dc0fbf9661d5, carrying .claude-plugin/ and skills/ directly at the root (no plugins/ subdirectory) -> skills subtree 24b1cbc1685248b1a3b2a30ffb2b854a43efd050, containing formal-verify, lean-model, proof-simplify, and tlaplus-model. .claude-plugin/plugin.json at the tag self-declares name proof-skills, version 0.1.1, author {name: Opum AI, url: https://github.com/opum-ai}, license MIT -- confirmed by direct GitHub API contents read, matching what opum-agent relayed. yaml-lsp.note: OMARK-79 (OPAG-960 AC3, DEC-109). First pin of a sixth entry, and the first whose recorded subtree is not skills/ -- yaml-lsp ships no skills directory, following the official -lsp pattern (the plugin folder carries only README and LICENSE; the manifest carries the server config), so the baseline records the .claude-plugin manifest subtree: the content that configures the plugin, and what a repointed tag would have to move to change its behaviour. Repo-root layout (.claude-plugin/ and evals/ directly at the root, no plugins/ subdirectory), so the existing github-source checkers and the Codex generator handle it without a code change, as OMARK-73 established for proof-skills. Tag chain resolved independently two ways and cross-checked: local `git rev-parse`/`ls-tree` (tag ref v0.1.0 -> annotated tag object 02dc66c66a2fc8d58d6f090c011ef55909bcfb12 -> peels to commit 887535a54b6dce4aa0750a72fd947ac31ccc4a6a, which is also the repository dev HEAD -> root tree b3258743a25bd3505914c623ea247664483ada25 -> .claude-plugin subtree c388fc784c1285bd7cec3d6eb8d4e3047d572585) and the GitHub git-database API (git/ref/tags -> git/tags -> git/commits -> git/trees), the exact path check-federated-content.mjs walks; `git ls-remote --tags` agrees (v0.1.0 and its ^{} peel line). .claude-plugin/plugin.json at the tag self-declares name yaml-lsp, version 0.1.0, license MIT, and the lspServers config (yaml-language-server --stdio; .yaml and .yml mapped to languageId yaml), confirmed by fetching the pin checker's own URL, raw.githubusercontent.com/opum-ai/yaml-lsp/v0.1.0/.claude-plugin/plugin.json. Placement measured on claude 2.1.286: with a manifest present the marketplace entry copy of lspServers is inert, and a live install from this entry's exact shape (github source, no inline config) registers the server -- component inventory reads `LSP servers (1)  yaml-language-server`, with version 0.1.0 resolved from the tag. The plugin's eval suite (evals/lsp-tool-answers-for-yaml, claude 2.1.286, 2026-10-01) passes at 1.00 with the plugin and 0.00 without it, delta 1.00, recorded in the plugin's own evals/BASELINE.md; the no-plugin arm has no LSP tool at all, so that delta is a plugin-fired signal rather than a style difference. The entry carries no lspServers inline by design: the manifest is the manifest, and the entry copy is inert once one exists.
